attachments.name: medical_plan.txt
attachments.text:
EVENT MEDICAL PLAN
Tanners Row Spring Dash 5K, Sunday 8 August 2027
Applicant: Tanners Row Business Association
Issue: 1.2

Runners get an email in race week telling them to dress for the weather and to keep a phone with them if they can. Most have run with us before. The list of entrants includes an emergency contact for each runner, which is kept at the start.

1. Event summary
A 5K race with 299 runners, starting at 08:00 in the Tanners Row area of Port Halden. An ambulance from Lifeline Event Medics is on site for the race; the paperwork is attached.

2. First aid cover
3 first aid posts will operate, at the start, at the finish and at the course midpoint, staffed by 8 qualified first aiders. Posts are placed so that no part of the course is more than 1.5 km from one. Two cycle responders move along the course with defibrillators.

3. Weather and hydration
Water is available every 2.5 km. The race director checks the forecast 48 hours and 2 hours before the start. Above 28 degrees C the start is brought forward or the course shortened, and above 32 degrees C the race is cancelled. In cold or wet conditions, foil blankets and a warm shelter are at the finish.

4. Transfer to hospital
The receiving hospital is Thornton County Hospital, 16 km from the finish. The transfer route and the pick-up point at the top of Foundry Street have been walked with the first aid team. The hospital's emergency department has been told the date and the expected numbers.

5. Communications
Every first aid post and cycle responder carries a radio on the medical channel, with phones as backup. All calls for an ambulance go through the medical lead, who gives the crew the access point and the nearest barrier to open.

6. Clinical lead
The medical lead is Fatima Haddad, a registered paramedic, who is on site from an hour before the start until the last runner is cleared. The lead can have any runner withdrawn on medical grounds.

attachments.name: race_plan.txt
attachments.text:
RACE PLAN
Tanners Row Spring Dash 5K | Sunday 8 August 2027
Organiser: Tanners Row Business Association
Race director: Patrick Doyle
Reference: RQ-35009

Overview
The Tanners Row Spring Dash 5K is a 5K race of 5 km for 299 entrants, based in the Tanners Row area of Port Halden. The start is at 08:00 and the course closes at 09:15.

Course
The course runs in order along Foundry Street, Harbour Boulevard, Salter Way, Bridge Row and Union Row, all of which are closed to traffic for the race. Major roads crossed: High Street, Prince Street, Dock Road and Canal Road. The finish is in Clocktower Square.

Course dimensions
Survey widths: Foundry Street 10 m, Bridge Row 16 m, Union Row 9 m, kerb to kerb, excluding footways. Start pens sit side by side across the full carriageway, and spectators have the pavement and a grassed verge along most of the route.

Support
Entrants collect numbers from the top of Foundry Street from one hour before the start. Timing is by chip, with mats at the start and finish. Results are posted on the Tanners Row website the same day.

attachments.name: traffic_plan.txt
attachments.text:
Traffic arrangements for the Tanners Row Spring Dash 5K, Sunday 8 August 2027

From Patrick Doyle, Volunteer Coordinator, Tanners Row Business Association

We have tried to think through what happens on the roads on race day. The race is a 5K, it starts at 08:00, and it goes through the Tanners Row area. See the attached correspondence from the police for the escort.

Closing the roads
We need the following closures, and Signal Hill Traffic Services will put out the barriers and signs for us. Foundry Street from Abbey Road to Brook Street, 06:30 until 09:45. Harbour Boulevard from Weir Street to Abbey Road, 06:30 until 09:45. Salter Way from Garrison Street to Weir Street, 06:30 until 09:45. Bridge Row from Brook Street to Tanner Street, 06:30 until 09:45. Union Row from Mill Road to Abbey Road, 06:30 until 09:45.

Crossings
Where we cross a major road we will have people stationed from 06:30 until the last runner is through. At High Street, where it meets Union Row, there will be 4 traffic marshals with stop/go boards and a supervisor. At Prince Street, where it meets Harbour Boulevard, there will be 2 traffic marshals with stop/go boards and a supervisor. At Dock Road, where it meets Foundry Street, there will be 4 traffic marshals with stop/go boards and a supervisor. At Canal Road, where it meets Foundry Street, there will be 4 traffic marshals with stop/go boards and a supervisor.

Getting around the closures
We've worked out the way round for drivers and Signal Hill Traffic Services will sign it. Traffic off Foundry Street goes via Ferry Road and Cross Avenue, signed from Tanner Street. Traffic off Harbour Boulevard goes via Victoria Road and Tram Street, signed from Weir Street. Traffic off Salter Way goes via Regent Road and Victoria Road, signed from Mill Road. Traffic off Bridge Row goes via Tram Street and Queen's Road, signed from Brook Street. Traffic off Union Row goes via Tram Street and Ferry Road, signed from Abbey Road.

Emergency vehicles
We keep one lane clear the whole way, 3.5 metres or more, for ambulances and fire engines. Every barrier has someone with a radio on our channel, and they can have it open within two minutes. Our controller on the day has direct numbers for police and ambulance control.

Letting people know
We put the race on our Facebook page and in the club newsletter, and the local paper usually gives us a mention.

We have a good working relationship with local residents. Several members walk the route the week before, noting anything that has changed, such as new roadworks, a barrier left in place, or a lane marked for cycles.

Afterwards
Our sweep vehicle follows the last runner, and each closure comes off in turn once it has passed and the road is clear. Everything will be open again by 09:45.
